body.statement: Suppose \(\Pr(q\in C_n)\ge1-\alpha_q\) and \(\Pr(\mathcal P\in\Pi_n)\ge1-\alpha_g\). Then the confidence fiber satisfies \(\Pr(\Theta_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\subseteq\widehat{\mathfrak C}_n)\ge1-\alpha_q-\alpha_g\) without differentiability, compactness, or a unique active optimizer. In the saturated binary witness, simultaneous one-sided exact binomial lower limits \(l_{01}\) and \(l_{00}\), each with error allocation \(\alpha_q/2\), yield the finite-sample interval \([\delta l_{01},1-\delta l_{00}]\) covering the entire sharp fiber with probability at least \(1-\alpha_q\).
body.justification: Finite-sample event inclusion remains valid at singular active faces, unattained endpoints, and collapsed identification intervals.
body.gap: Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer treat a fixed criterion, Imbens and Manski treat interval endpoints, and Chang, Guo, and Malinsky treat post-discovery point effects; none covers a learned selection-COPAG compatibility fiber.
body.consumer: The method attaches calibrated uncertainty to the graph and effect ambiguity in the survivor-selected cardiac-surgery FCI and LV-IDA analysis.
